reason: The cited evidence (E1) examines structural and magnetic properties of (MgCoNiCuZnMn)O and (MgCoNiCuZnCr)O thin films, which are oxide systems unrelated to the metallic FeMnNiGeSi alloy in the hypothesis. It provides no support for any of the key premises regarding strain, domain wall pinning, annealing effects, or magnetocaloric response in the proposed material system.
premises: Finite-size induced interfacial strain and defect-induced domain wall pinning govern magnetocaloric response and hysteresis in nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi alloys.
Post-deposition annealing relaxes interfacial stresses and reduces defect density in these alloys.
Reduced pinning centers from annealing lead to smoother magnetic domain motion and reduced hysteresis.
Reduced hysteresis and relaxed strain partially restore bulk-like magnetocaloric performance in nanoscale forms.
Heat-transfer limits become less critical as thermal gradients are reduced by relaxed strain.
